sources.title: Runbook: Atlas Database Failover
sources.content:
When to Use

Use this runbook when the primary Atlas PostgreSQL cluster in Frankfurt is unavailable or read-only for more than 10 minutes and Cobalt Cloud cannot give a recovery estimate within that time. Revised on 2 April 2026 for platform version 4.2 after the March outage (action item ATL-1121), and tested in the Q2 and Q3 2026 drills.

Targets

Recovery point objective: 5 minutes. Recovery time objective: 30 minutes. These targets appear in the Halvorsen Logistics MSA, so every failover must be recorded for client reporting.

Roles

- Incident commander: coordinates and decides go/no-go for promotion.
- Operator: runs the commands in this runbook.
- Communications lead: updates the status page within 15 minutes and every 30 minutes after, and emails Halvorsen's operations team hourly.

One person must not hold more than one role during a Severity 1 incident.

Pre-Checks

1. Declare a Severity 1 incident in PagerDuty and page the incident commander on duty.
2. Open a Priority 1 ticket with Cobalt Cloud support, quoting enterprise agreement CC-ENT-4471. Record the Cobalt incident reference; finance needs it to claim a Service Credit.
3. Check Cobalt's status portal for the Frankfurt region and note the start time of the incident.
4. In Grafana, confirm replication lag on the Dubai replica is under 5 minutes. If it is higher, the incident commander decides whether to wait or accept the data loss, and records the decision.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
Detection and Response Metrics

| Metric | Target | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Time to page (alert to on-call paged) | 2 minutes | 1 minute |
| Time to acknowledge (Severity 1) | 15 minutes | 4 minutes |
| Time to first status page update | 15 minutes | 52 minutes |
| Time to first client email to Halvorsen | 30 minutes | 45 minutes |
| Time to restore (recovery time objective) | 30 minutes | 220 minutes |
| Data loss (recovery point objective) | 5 minutes | 0 minutes (47 seconds of lag, replayed) |

The recovery time objective of 30 minutes in the Halvorsen MSA was missed by more than three hours. The MSA treats the recovery objectives as targets rather than as commitments that carry Service Credits, but the miss was reported to Halvorsen in the written incident report as required by clause 7.3 of the MSA.

Client Communications Log

- 06:55 Phone call from Bilal Ahmed to Ingrid Solberg, Head of Data at Halvorsen Logistics.
- 06:55 Email to Halvorsen's operations analytics manager, Jonas Eriksen.
- 07:10 First status page update for all clients.
- 08:00, 09:00 Hourly updates to Halvorsen by email, as required during a Severity 1 incident.
- 09:55 Recovery confirmed to all clients by email and status page.
- 24 March 2026 Written incident report sent to Halvorsen, within the ten Business Days required by the MSA.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
**Could we have avoided the outage entirely?** Not the storage failure, which was Cobalt's. But with an up-to-date runbook and a recent drill, recovery would probably have taken about 30 minutes instead of 220.

**Did we breach the Halvorsen MSA?** No. Availability stayed above 99.5%. We missed the 30-minute recovery time objective, which the MSA states as a target, and we reported that openly.

**What would it take to fail over automatically?** Automatic promotion would need a reliable way to decide that Frankfurt is truly down, to avoid two primaries. The platform team recommends finishing multi-zone placement first, which addresses the most likely failure mode, and revisiting automatic failover in 2027.

**Does this affect the Cobalt renewal?** Yes. The renewal term sheet now asks for multi-zone placement for managed PostgreSQL at no extra charge and a 60-day Service Credit claim window.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
SLA Calculations > Atlas Availability for Halvorsen

March 2026 had 31 days, which is 44,640 minutes. Downtime was 220 minutes. Availability was therefore (44,640 − 220) ÷ 44,640 = 99.507%, reported as 99.51%. The Halvorsen MSA threshold is 99.5%, so no Service Credit was due. The largest outage that would have stayed above 99.5% in March is 223 minutes.

SLA Calculations > Cobalt Cloud Availability for Acme

Cobalt measured Frankfurt region availability at 99.51% for March. The CC-ENT-4471 threshold is 99.9%, so the Frankfurt region earned the 10% Service Credit tier (below 99.9% but at least 99.0%). March's Frankfurt Regional Fees were EUR 16,500, so the credit was EUR 1,650. The Dubai and London regions were unaffected and earned no credit.

Follow-Up Failover Drills > Q2 2026 Drill (12 May 2026)

The rewritten runbook was used to fail Atlas over from Frankfurt to Dubai in a planned drill during the Sunday maintenance window. Failover completed in 19 minutes, inside the 30-minute recovery time objective. One issue was found: the configuration service cached the old database endpoint for five minutes. The cache time was reduced to 30 seconds.

Follow-Up Failover Drills > Q3 2026 Drill (9 August 2026)

The drill was run by a newer engineer who had never performed a failover, to test whether the runbook could be followed without help. Failover completed in 24 minutes. The drill summary was shared with Halvorsen Logistics, as the MSA requires on request.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
What Happened

On Saturday 14 March 2026, Atlas was unavailable to all clients for 3 hours 40 minutes (220 minutes), from 06:10 to 09:50 UTC. The incident was classified Severity 1. The incident commander was Bilal Ahmed, with Mei Lin Zhou (CTO) as the executive on call.

Why It Happened

A storage incident in Cobalt Cloud's Frankfurt region made the primary Atlas PostgreSQL cluster read-only. The team tried to fail over to the disaster recovery replica in the Dubai region, but the database failover runbook was out of date: it referenced a replication setting that had been renamed in the January 2026 platform upgrade. Working out the correct procedure under pressure took about two hours.

Status

This postmortem is blameless. All action items are tracked in Jira under the epic ATL-1120. As of 30 June 2026, five of seven action items are complete.

sources.title: Atlas Platform Architecture
sources.content:
Deployment

Code is hosted in GitHub Enterprise and deployed by GitHub Actions. Production deployments need one approving review and run only between 10:00 and 16:00 PKT on weekdays. Platform upgrades follow a checklist that, since April 2026, includes reviewing every runbook affected by the change.

Security

All data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Production access requires SSO with hardware-key multi-factor authentication. Access is reviewed quarterly by the platform team. An independent penetration test of Atlas is commissioned every year, as required by client contracts and by Acme's ISO 27001 certification.

Recovery

The database failover runbook describes how to promote the Dubai replica. Failover drills run every quarter; the Q2 2026 drill completed in 19 minutes and the Q3 2026 drill in 24 minutes, both within the 30-minute recovery time objective.

Known Limitations

- Single-zone primary database until ATL-1125 is complete.
- Staging database configuration differs from production (ATL-1127, not started).
- Cross-region failover is manual; there is no automatic promotion.

sources.title: ISO 27001 Recertification Audit Plan 2027
sources.content:
Audit Details

Acme's ISO 27001 recertification audit will be carried out by the certification body Nordcert from 15 to 19 February 2027. The audit covers all three offices (Karachi, Dubai and London) and the Atlas platform. Audit lead on Acme's side: Tomás Ferreira, General Counsel. Technical lead: Mei Lin Zhou, CTO. Acme has held ISO 27001 certification since 2019; the current certificate expires on 28 February 2027.

Audit Fee

Nordcert's audit fee is EUR 24,000, under contract NC-ACME-2027. The 2026 budget includes USD 26,000 for the audit, which covers the fee and auditor travel.

Preconditions

Before the audit:

- Every active client contract must have a current data processing addendum (DPA) listing the subprocessors actually in use.
- Every vendor processing client data must have an in-force agreement on the audit dates.
- Any contract that expires before the audit must either be renewed or have a documented exit plan.
- Every critical vendor must have a named business owner and a current security review.

Why the Cobalt Renewal Is Critical

Cobalt Cloud hosts Atlas and the Brightwater Health workloads. If the Cobalt agreement lapses on 31 December 2026 with no renewal, Acme would have no in-force hosting agreement during the audit, which would be a major nonconformity. The legal team has therefore set an internal deadline of 30 November 2026 for signature, leaving a month of contingency.

Halvorsen DPA Update

The Halvorsen DPA was last updated in March 2024. Its subprocessor list (Cobalt Cloud, Ledgerline Software, Grafana Labs) is still accurate, but its description of the disaster recovery region and the breach notification timelines must be re-confirmed after the March 2026 outage. The updated DPA should be signed together with the renewal confirmation.

sources.title: Acme Advisory Group — Company Overview
sources.content:
Who We Are

Acme Advisory Group is a management and technology consulting firm founded in 2011 in Karachi by Sara Qureshi and Daniel Okafor. Sara Qureshi serves as Chief Executive Officer and Daniel Okafor as Chief Financial Officer. The firm employs approximately 240 people across three offices: Karachi (headquarters), Dubai and London.

Practices

Acme is organised into three practices:

- Digital Transformation, led by Farah Naqvi, which redesigns operating models and customer journeys.
- Cloud Advisory, led by Mei Lin Zhou, who is also the firm's Chief Technology Officer. This practice runs Atlas, our managed client analytics platform.
- Risk and Compliance, led by Tomás Ferreira, who is also General Counsel. This practice helps clients prepare for ISO 27001 and SOC 2.

Clients and Sectors

We serve mid-sized organisations in logistics, healthcare and insurance. Our longest-running managed service is the Atlas analytics service for a European logistics client. Client names are confidential and are not published outside the firm.

Certifications

Acme has held ISO 27001 certification since 2019. The next recertification audit is scheduled for February 2027.

| Chief Financial Officer | Daniel Okafor |

sources.title: Code Of Conduct
sources.content:
Acme Advisory Group expects every employee to act with integrity, respect and care for client confidentiality.

Gifts and hospitality: employees may accept gifts worth up to USD 50. Anything above USD 50 must be declared to the compliance team within five business days and may need to be returned.

Conflicts of interest: any personal or financial relationship with a client, supplier or competitor must be declared to your line manager and the General Counsel before you work on a related engagement.

Confidentiality: client information may only be shared with colleagues who need it for their work. Client data must stay within approved systems.

Speaking up: concerns can be raised confidentially with the General Counsel, Tomás Ferreira, or through the anonymous ethics line. Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith is a disciplinary offence.

Breaches of this code may lead to disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.

sources.title: Acme Service Catalog
sources.content:
Cloud Readiness Assessment

A four-week, fixed-fee engagement that reviews a client's applications, data and security posture and produces a migration roadmap. Delivered by the Cloud Advisory practice. Typical team: one manager and two consultants.

Atlas Managed Analytics

Atlas is Acme's managed analytics platform. Clients receive dashboards, data pipelines and a monthly insights review. Atlas is billed as a monthly subscription with a 99.5% availability commitment. Onboarding a new Atlas client takes six to eight weeks.

Cloud Migration Programmes

Multi-month programmes that move client workloads to the cloud. These are contracted under a Statement of Work (SOW) with milestone-based fees. Data residency requirements are agreed in the SOW before work starts.

Compliance Advisory

Gap assessments and remediation support for ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II. A gap assessment takes three weeks. Remediation support is billed on a time-and-materials basis at the consultant day rates published to clients each January.

Digital Operating Model Design

Workshops and design sprints that redesign how a client's teams work. Usually six to ten weeks.

How to Engage Us

New enquiries go to the engagement desk. A partner responds within two business days. Every engagement starts with a signed Master Services Agreement or a Statement of Work.

sources.content:
Karachi (Headquarters)

Floor 7, Crescent Business Centre, Karachi. Around 150 staff. The Karachi office hosts the Digital Transformation practice, the People team and the finance team. Reception is staffed from 8:30 to 18:30.

Level 12, Harbour Tower, Dubai Marina. Around 55 staff. Home of the Cloud Advisory practice and the Atlas operations team. The Dubai office also hosts the secondary Atlas operations room used during failover exercises.

Visiting Another Office

Staff visiting another office should book a desk through the facilities page at least two business days in advance. Building access cards are issued by the receiving office's facilities coordinator.

sources.title: Employee FAQ
sources.content:
What are standard office hours?

Core hours are 9:00 to 18:00 local time, Monday to Friday, in all three offices. Friday prayers are accommodated in Karachi and Dubai with a 12:30 to 14:00 break.

How do I get IT help?

Raise a ticket in Beacon, the internal IT helpdesk portal. Urgent issues (you cannot work at all) can also be reported to the IT hotline extension 4357. Beacon tickets are answered within four business hours.

How do I book business travel?

Travel is booked through the finance team using the travel request form in Ledgerline. Requests need line-manager approval before booking. See the Expense Policy for travel class rules.

Where are company policies kept?

All policies are published on the intranet under "Policies". HR policies such as leave and remote work are also in PeopleDesk, the HR portal.

Who do I contact about payroll?

Payroll questions go to the People team through PeopleDesk. Payslips are published on the 25th of each month.

Can I use personal devices for work?

Only for email and chat through the approved mobile apps, and only with device encryption and a screen lock enabled. Client data must never be stored on personal devices.

sources.title: Runbook: Ledger Vault Backup and Restore
sources.content:
Purpose

This runbook describes how Ledger Vault is backed up and how to restore it, either after data loss or to fail over to the Frankfurt disaster recovery region. It is owned by Kwame Mensah, Head of IT.

Backups > Database

The Ledger Vault metadata database is backed up nightly at 01:00 PKT. Backups are kept for 35 days. Each backup is encrypted with a Globex-managed key and copied to Tessera Cloud's Frankfurt region.

Backups > Files

Client file storage uses object versioning with 90-day retention. UK client files in the London bucket are versioned in the London region only and are never copied to Frankfurt, so that they stay in the UK.

Backups > Targets

Recovery point objective: 24 hours. Recovery time objective: 4 hours.

When to Restore

- Data loss or corruption in the metadata database.
- Accidental deletion of a client folder beyond what versioning can recover.
- The Bahrain region is unavailable and Tessera cannot give a recovery estimate within one hour, in which case a restore into Frankfurt is considered.

The Head of IT decides whether to restore. During busy season (15 January to 31 March) the decision should be made quickly, because audit deadlines depend on Ledger Vault.

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Why a Full Disk Stopped the Whole Application

Ledger Vault writes a session record and an audit log entry for every page view, so even read-only actions such as viewing a file list need a database write. When the disk filled, every request failed, not only uploads. A later design change, scheduled for 2027, will move session storage to an in-memory store so that read-only browsing can continue during database write failures.

Why Recovery Took So Long After the Resize

After the resize at 12:22, the database had to replay its write-ahead log and run integrity checks across tables that had grown quickly during busy season. Recovery took 2 hours 28 minutes. Tessera's root cause analysis noted that recovery would have been about 40 minutes if the database had been resized before it filled, because no crash recovery would have been needed.

What Was in the 500 GB

| Data | Size on 30 March 2026 |
|---|---|
| File metadata and permissions | 118 GB |
| Version history records | 196 GB |
| Audit log entries | 141 GB |
| Session records | 40 GB (expired sessions, deleted during the incident) |
| Indexes and other | 5 GB |

Audit log entries are kept for seven years for regulatory reasons. The IT team is planning to move audit log entries older than one year to cheaper archive storage in 2027, with Albion Assurance Certification's agreement that this still meets ISO 27001 logging requirements.

sources.title: Ledger Vault Platform Architecture
sources.content:
Components > Fernbook Connector

Fernbook, the audit working-paper platform supplied by Fernbook Ltd, links to Ledger Vault files through an API connector maintained by the IT team. When an auditor attaches evidence in Fernbook, the connector stores a reference to the Ledger Vault file rather than a copy.

Availability and Recovery

Ledger Vault targets 99.9% availability, with a recovery point objective of 24 hours and a recovery time objective of 4 hours. Disaster recovery to Frankfurt is performed by restoring the latest backup into a new environment, following the backup and restore runbook. In March 2026 availability was 99.17% because of the 370-minute outage.

Monitoring and On-Call > Alerts

Alerts for database storage, failed uploads, application errors and certificate expiry are routed to the IT on-call phone and the IT team mailbox. Before April 2026 alerts went only to the mailbox.

Monitoring and On-Call > IT On-Call Rotation

The IT on-call rotation changes every Wednesday at 09:00 PKT. Sev1 incidents must be acknowledged within 20 minutes and Sev2 within one hour. Unresolved Sev1 incidents are escalated after 45 minutes to Kwame Mensah. The on-call allowance is PKR 12,000 per week. When the hosting platform is at fault, the on-call engineer raises a Priority 1 ticket with Tessera, quoting TC-7720; urgent resize requests are raised as Priority 1 whenever the service is down.

sources.title: Runbook: Ledger Vault Backup and Restore
sources.content:
Example: Recovering a Deleted Client Folder

During busy season an engagement manager deletes the wrong folder for a Sunridge Schools Trust tax engagement. The IT service desk first restores the files from object versioning, which keeps deleted versions for 90 days. Folder permissions were also removed, so IT restores the previous night's database backup to a temporary instance, exports the permission records for that folder and re-imports them into production. The full production database is not restored. The engagement manager confirms the restored folder with the client's financial controller, and the incident is logged as a Sev3.

Contacts

| Who | When |
|---|---|
| Kwame Mensah, Head of IT | Any decision to restore; Sev1 escalation after 45 minutes |
| Tessera Cloud support (TC-7720) | Infrastructure faults, resizes; Priority 1 when Ledger Vault is down |
| Engagement partners | Within 30 minutes of a Sev1 affecting Ledger Vault |
| Finance team | Same day, with the Tessera ticket reference, for Service Credit claims within 15 days |
| Henrik Dahl, Legal Counsel | Any suspected loss or exposure of client data |

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Impact > Contractual Impact

Ledger Vault's availability for March 2026 was 99.17% (44,640 minutes in the month, 370 minutes of downtime). Tessera Cloud's agreement TC-7720 commits to 99.95% monthly availability, with a Service Credit of 15% of the USD 15,000 Monthly Fee when availability falls below 99.5%. Claims must be filed within 15 days of the incident.

Timeline (all times PKT) > Build-Up

- 23 to 29 March: client uploads run at three times the normal daily volume as busy season closes. Metadata database storage rises from 71% to 94%.
- 29 March, 22:40: database storage reaches 95%. An alert is emailed to the IT team mailbox, which is not monitored overnight. No page is sent.

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
**Should Globex keep Ledger Vault in-house?** The partners agreed to keep Ledger Vault, because it gives clients a single secure place to share evidence and integrates with Fernbook, but asked IT to report on the renewal options with Tessera before the notice deadline of 30 January 2027.

**Could clients have been told sooner?** Yes. The first client communication was at 13:30, more than four hours into the outage. The IT on-call guide now requires engagement partners to be informed within 30 minutes of a Sev1 affecting Ledger Vault, so they can contact clients with imminent deadlines.

**Was any client data at risk?** No. The failure prevented writes but did not corrupt or expose data. The Legal Counsel confirmed that no client notification under the engagement letters' breach clauses was needed.

**What happens if this repeats during the 2027 busy season?** Automatic scaling, earlier alerts and the December capacity review should prevent a repeat. If Ledger Vault is unavailable for more than four hours during final fieldwork, engagement letters such as Marlowe's now allow a temporary encrypted transfer approved by the Head of IT, keeping UK files in the UK.

On your first day you receive a firm laptop, a Microsoft 365 account with single sign-on through Microsoft Entra ID, access to Ledger Vault (our client document portal) and an introduction to Fernbook, our audit working-paper platform. Each joiner is assigned a counselling partner who supports their development throughout their time at Globex.

As an audit firm we must be independent of our audit clients. All new joiners complete an independence declaration on day one, listing financial interests (shares, loans, insurance policies) and close family relationships with any client or client director. You must update your declaration within five working days of any change, and confirm it every year in June.

2. Joining Globex > 2.3 Probation

Probation lasts six months. Your counselling partner and line manager hold a review at three months and at the end of probation. During probation, either side may end employment with two weeks' notice.

In your first month you must complete information security, anti-money laundering and Fernbook fundamentals training. Audit staff must also complete the firm's audit methodology course before their first busy season.

Office hours are 9:30 to 17:30 local time, Monday to Friday.

sources.title: Runbook: On-Call Rotation
sources.content:
Purpose

The platform on-call engineer protects Atlas availability outside and inside business hours. This runbook explains the rotation, response times, escalation and pay.

Rotation

The platform on-call rotation changes every Monday at 10:00 PKT. Each engineer is on call for one week at a time, at most one week in every four. The schedule is maintained in PagerDuty. Engineers swap shifts in PagerDuty and tell the platform lead; swaps must be in place before the shift starts.

Before Your Shift

- Check that PagerDuty can reach you by phone call and push notification.
- Confirm your hardware security key works for production access.
- Read the handover notes from the previous engineer.
- Make sure you can reach a laptop and a reliable internet connection within 15 minutes at all times.

Severity Levels and Response Times

| Severity | Definition | Acknowledge within |
|---|---|---|
| Sev1 | Atlas down for all clients, or data loss risk | 15 minutes |
| Sev2 | Major feature broken, or one client fully down | 30 minutes |
| Sev3 | Minor issue with a workaround | Next business day |

The Halvorsen Logistics MSA requires Acme to acknowledge Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes and Severity 2 incidents within two hours. Our internal targets are stricter so that we meet the contract with margin.

sources.title: Runbook: On-Call Rotation
sources.content:
| Who | When |
|---|---|
| Incident commander on duty (PagerDuty schedule) | Every Sev1, and Sev2 lasting over an hour |
| Mei Lin Zhou, CTO | Sev1 unresolved after 30 minutes |
| Security lead and Tomás Ferreira, General Counsel | Any suspected security breach |
| Cobalt Cloud support (CC-ENT-4471) | Infrastructure faults; Priority 1 response in 15 minutes |
| Finance team | Same day, with Cobalt incident references for Service Credit claims |

sources.title: Runbook: On-Call Rotation
sources.content:
Handling an Incident

1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty.
2. Open an incident channel in Slack and post what you know.
3. For a Sev1, page the incident commander on duty immediately. The incident commander appoints a communications lead, who updates the status page within 15 minutes.
4. If the cause is Cobalt Cloud infrastructure, open a Priority 1 ticket with Cobalt support quoting CC-ENT-4471. Cobalt's first response target for Priority 1 is 15 minutes.
5. If the primary database is unavailable for more than 10 minutes, follow the database failover runbook.
6. Record every action and its time in the incident channel.

Escalation

If the on-call engineer cannot resolve a Sev1 within 30 minutes, escalate to the incident commander on duty, then to Mei Lin Zhou (CTO). For incidents that may involve a security breach, also page the security lead and inform Tomás Ferreira (General Counsel), because client contracts require breach notification within 48 hours.

Allowance and Time Off

Engineers receive an on-call allowance of PKR 15,000 per week on call, paid with the next month's salary. Engineers also receive time off in lieu for any incident handled between midnight and 06:00, equal to the time spent plus one hour, to be taken within a month.

Handover

At handover, the outgoing engineer posts a summary of open incidents, alerts that fired, and anything unusual in the platform channel, and tags the incoming engineer. The incoming engineer acknowledges the handover before 10:30 PKT.

Acme Advisory Group expects every employee to act with integrity, respect and care for client confidentiality.

Gifts and hospitality: employees may accept gifts worth up to USD 50. Anything above USD 50 must be declared to the compliance team within five business days and may need to be returned.

Workshops and design sprints that redesign how a client's teams work. Usually six to ten weeks.

New enquiries go to the engagement desk. A partner responds within two business days. Every engagement starts with a signed Master Services Agreement or a Statement of Work.

sources.title: Leave Policy
sources.content:
Scope

This policy applies to all employees of Globex Partners LLP in Lahore, Abu Dhabi and Manchester. Partners follow the partnership agreement. Where local law gives a more generous entitlement, local law applies. The policy is owned by Aisha Farooq, HR Director, and summarised in the Staff Handbook.

Annual Leave > Entitlement

Full-time employees receive 25 working days of paid annual leave per year. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement. Employees who join or leave during the year receive a pro-rata entitlement for the months worked.

Annual Leave > Carryover

Up to 10 unused days may be carried over into the next year. Carried-over days must be used by 30 June, after busy season, or they are forfeited. Days above the carryover limit are not paid out except on leaving.

Annual Leave > Busy Season Restriction

From 15 January to 31 March, annual leave of more than three consecutive days needs approval from the engagement partner. Engagement partners approve such leave only for weddings, family emergencies or leave booked before the employee joined Globex. Leave of up to three days during busy season needs only line manager approval.

Annual Leave > Requesting Leave

Leave is requested through the HR system and approved by the line manager, normally within three working days. Requests for more than five consecutive days should be made at least four weeks in advance. Audit staff should also tell the engagement manager of every engagement they are booked on, so that client fieldwork is not affected.

Annual Leave > Leave After Busy Season

Globex encourages staff to take at least five consecutive days of leave between April and June each year. Staff who worked Saturdays in busy season also take their time off in lieu in this period.

Sick Leave > Entitlement

Employees receive 12 days of paid sick leave per year. Sick leave does not carry over.

The platform team wants a new log analysis tool that will receive Atlas application logs, which may contain client user names. The annual cost is USD 14,000, so three quotes are needed. sources.title: Procurement Policy
sources.content:
Purpose and Scope

This policy makes sure Acme buys goods and services at fair prices, from vendors that protect client data, with contracts that meet Acme's obligations to its clients. It applies to all purchases by all offices. It is owned by Daniel Okafor, CFO.

Purchase Requests

Every purchase above USD 1,000 starts with a purchase request in Ledgerline, stating the need, the budget line and the expected annual cost. Purchases below USD 1,000 may be made on a company card and claimed through the expense process.

Quotes

Purchases above USD 10,000 require three written quotes, unless the vendor is the only supplier able to meet the requirement, which must be justified in writing and approved by the CFO. Quotes and the justification are attached to the purchase request in Ledgerline.

Security Review > When a Review Is Needed

Any vendor that will store or process client data needs a vendor security review by the platform team before the contract is signed. Vendors that only receive system metrics or billing contact data need a lighter review.

Security Review > What the Review Covers

The review covers certifications (such as ISO 27001 or SOC 2), data location, encryption, access controls, incident history and the vendor's own subprocessors. The platform team records the outcome and the review date in the vendor register.

Security Review > Client Obligations

Some client contracts restrict which subprocessors Acme may use. The Halvorsen Logistics MSA requires 30 days' notice to Halvorsen before adding or replacing any subprocessor that handles Halvorsen's data, and Brightwater Health Trust must consent in writing to any new subprocessor with access to its data. The legal team checks client contracts before any such vendor is signed.

sources.content:
Contract Requirements

Contracts with vendors that process client data must include:

- a data processing agreement;
- security incident notification within 24 hours, so Acme can meet client notification commitments such as the 48-hour commitment to Halvorsen;

- Contracts of USD 50,000 per year or more: Chief Financial Officer.

The Cobalt Cloud enterprise agreement, with committed spend of EUR 264,000 a year, was signed by the CFO under this rule.

Critical Vendors

A vendor is critical if a client service depends on it. Critical vendors need a named business owner, an exit plan and a renewal review at least 120 days before the contract ends. Current critical vendors are Cobalt Cloud (hosting) and Ledgerline (invoicing).

Renewals

The business owner starts each renewal review at least 120 days before the contract end date for critical vendors, and at least 60 days before for other vendors. Renewals follow the same quote and signature rules as new contracts, except that the three-quote rule may be waived for critical vendors where switching would put client services at risk, with the CFO's approval.

Every signed contract is added to the vendor register by the finance team within five business days of signature, with the contract reference, business owner, annual value, end date and criticality.

Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy require written approval from the CFO, recorded in Ledgerline.

sources.title: Master Services Agreement — Halvorsen Logistics AS
sources.content:
Schedule 2 — Availability and Service Credits > S2.1 Measurement

Availability is measured by Acme's external monitoring, which checks the dashboard login page and a sample dashboard from two locations every minute. A minute counts as downtime when both checks fail from both locations. Availability for a month is the number of minutes in the month minus downtime minutes, divided by the number of minutes in the month, excluding planned maintenance.

Schedule 2 — Availability and Service Credits > S2.2 Service Credit Table

| Monthly availability | Service Credit (% of that month's Monthly Fee) |
|---|---|
| 99.5% or higher | No credit |
| Below 99.5% but at least 99.0% | 5% |
| Below 99.0% | 15% |

Schedule 2 — Availability and Service Credits > S2.3 Cap and Claims

Service Credits in any month are capped at 25% of that month's Monthly Fee. The Client must claim a Service Credit within 60 days of the end of the month concerned.

Schedule 2 — Availability and Service Credits > S2.4 Worked Example

In a 31-day month there are 44,640 minutes. An outage of 220 minutes gives availability of 99.51%, which is above 99.5%, so no Service Credit is due. An outage of 250 minutes gives availability of 99.44%, which earns a Service Credit of 5% of the Monthly Fee.

Schedule 3 — Day Rates

Additional work under a Statement of Work, and exit assistance beyond the standard export, is charged at the following day rates: Partner EUR 2,400; Director EUR 1,900; Manager EUR 1,400; Senior Consultant EUR 1,100; Consultant EUR 850. Day rates are fixed until 31 January 2027.

sources.title: Ledger Vault Platform Architecture
sources.content:
Components > Fernbook Connector

Fernbook, the audit working-paper platform supplied by Fernbook Ltd, links to Ledger Vault files through an API connector maintained by the IT team. When an auditor attaches evidence in Fernbook, the connector stores a reference to the Ledger Vault file rather than a copy.

Availability and Recovery

Ledger Vault targets 99.9% availability, with a recovery point objective of 24 hours and a recovery time objective of 4 hours. Disaster recovery to Frankfurt is performed by restoring the latest backup into a new environment, following the backup and restore runbook. In March 2026 availability was 99.17% because of the 370-minute outage.

Monitoring and On-Call > Alerts

Alerts for database storage, failed uploads, application errors and certificate expiry are routed to the IT on-call phone and the IT team mailbox. Before April 2026 alerts went only to the mailbox.

Monitoring and On-Call > IT On-Call Rotation

The IT on-call rotation changes every Wednesday at 09:00 PKT. Sev1 incidents must be acknowledged within 20 minutes and Sev2 within one hour. Unresolved Sev1 incidents are escalated after 45 minutes to Kwame Mensah. The on-call allowance is PKR 12,000 per week. When the hosting platform is at fault, the on-call engineer raises a Priority 1 ticket with Tessera, quoting TC-7720; urgent resize requests are raised as Priority 1 whenever the service is down.

sources.title: Ledger Vault Platform Architecture
sources.content:
IT Tooling Inventory

| Tool | Purpose | Owner | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tessera Cloud | Hosting for Ledger Vault (Bahrain, Frankfurt, London) | Kwame Mensah | TC-7720 |
| Fernbook | Audit working papers | Audit methodology team | Fernbook Ltd, FB-GLX-22 |
| Microsoft 365 and Entra ID | Email, documents, staff SSO | IT team | Enterprise agreement |
| Claimly | Expense claims | Finance | Annual subscription |
| Ledger Vault | Client document portal | IT team | Built in-house |

New tools that store client data need approval from the Head of IT and the Legal Counsel before purchase.

Security

All client data is encrypted at rest with Globex-managed keys and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher. Access to client folders is limited to the engagement team. Tessera must notify Globex of security incidents within 12 hours. Ledger Vault requires a separate login from email, which is why no client files were exposed in the August 2026 phishing incident.

Capacity Planning

A capacity review runs every December before busy season (15 January to 31 March), when uploads peak at about three times the normal volume. The first review is scheduled for December 2026.

Known Limitations

- Failover to Frankfurt is a manual restore, so the recovery time is hours rather than minutes.
- The Tessera agreement renews automatically on 31 March 2027 unless notice is given by 30 January 2027; the renewal decision is pending.
- Fernbook's contract (FB-GLX-22) ends on 31 December 2026, and the connector must be re-tested after any Fernbook upgrade.

sources.title: Ledger Vault Platform Architecture
sources.content:
Overview

Ledger Vault is Globex's secure client document portal. Clients upload trial balances, contracts and audit evidence, and audit teams link those files to working papers in Fernbook. The technical owner is Kwame Mensah, Head of IT. Ledger Vault is built and run in-house by the IT team.

Hosting > Provider

Ledger Vault is hosted on Tessera Cloud under agreement TC-7720 (USD 15,000 per month, term to 31 March 2027). Tessera commits to 99.95% monthly availability in the Bahrain region.

Hosting > Regions

- Bahrain: primary region for the application, the metadata database and most client files.
- Frankfurt: disaster recovery region, holding encrypted nightly backups.
- London: a dedicated storage bucket for UK client files, such as Marlowe Retail Group's, which must stay in the UK.

Components > Web Application

The Ledger Vault web application runs on Tessera virtual machines behind a managed web application firewall. Staff sign in with Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on and number-matching multi-factor authentication. Clients sign in with an email one-time passcode.

Components > Metadata Database

A managed PostgreSQL database stores file records, versions, permissions, sessions and audit log entries. Since the 30 March 2026 outage, automatic storage scaling is enabled (scaling at 80% usage in 25% steps), and storage alerts fire at 75% and 85%.

Components > Object Storage

Client files are stored in object storage with versioning enabled and 90-day version retention.

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Appendix C — Glossary

- Metadata database: the PostgreSQL database that stores file records, versions, permissions and sessions for Ledger Vault. Client files themselves are in object storage.
- Write-ahead log: the database's record of changes, replayed during recovery.
- Busy season: 15 January to 31 March, when most December year-end audits are completed.
- TC-7720: Globex's agreement reference with Tessera Cloud.
- TES-55190: Tessera's ticket reference for the urgent resize request.

Appendix D — Text of the Client Apology (31 March 2026)

"Dear client, on Monday 30 March, Ledger Vault, our secure document portal, was unavailable from 09:05 to 15:15 Pakistan time. During that period you could not upload or view documents, and our audit teams could not access evidence. No documents were lost, and documents you tried to upload during the outage should now be uploaded again. The cause was a storage capacity issue in our hosting environment, which has now been fixed, and we have added automatic capacity scaling and earlier warnings so that it cannot happen in the same way again. Where this affected your audit timetable, your engagement partner will contact you directly. We apologise for the disruption at the busiest time of the year. Imran Siddiqui, Managing Partner."

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
**Should Globex keep Ledger Vault in-house?** The partners agreed to keep Ledger Vault, because it gives clients a single secure place to share evidence and integrates with Fernbook, but asked IT to report on the renewal options with Tessera before the notice deadline of 30 January 2027.

**Could clients have been told sooner?** Yes. The first client communication was at 13:30, more than four hours into the outage. The IT on-call guide now requires engagement partners to be informed within 30 minutes of a Sev1 affecting Ledger Vault, so they can contact clients with imminent deadlines.

**Was any client data at risk?** No. The failure prevented writes but did not corrupt or expose data. The Legal Counsel confirmed that no client notification under the engagement letters' breach clauses was needed.

**What happens if this repeats during the 2027 busy season?** Automatic scaling, earlier alerts and the December capacity review should prevent a repeat. If Ledger Vault is unavailable for more than four hours during final fieldwork, engagement letters such as Marlowe's now allow a temporary encrypted transfer approved by the Head of IT, keeping UK files in the UK.

Schedule L — Fee Structure Health Check: Detailed Findings > L.1 Transport Fees

Several schools invoiced transport fees as part of a single "tuition and services" line. Because transport services may be treated differently from tuition for sales tax on services, combining them created a risk of under-declaring tax on the transport element. Recommendation: invoice transport fees as a separate line from the 2026–27 academic year. Status: implemented for invoices issued from August 2026.

Scholarships were granted by school principals without written criteria. Without documented criteria, the tax treatment of scholarship discounts could be challenged. Recommendation: adopt a board-approved scholarship policy with eligibility criteria and record each award. Status: policy approved by the board in April 2026.

sources.title: Code Of Conduct
sources.content:
Acme Advisory Group expects every employee to act with integrity, respect and care for client confidentiality.

Gifts and hospitality: employees may accept gifts worth up to USD 50. Anything above USD 50 must be declared to the compliance team within five business days and may need to be returned.

Conflicts of interest: any personal or financial relationship with a client, supplier or competitor must be declared to your line manager and the General Counsel before you work on a related engagement.

Confidentiality: client information may only be shared with colleagues who need it for their work. Client data must stay within approved systems.

Speaking up: concerns can be raised confidentially with the General Counsel, Tomás Ferreira, or through the anonymous ethics line. Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith is a disciplinary offence.

Breaches of this code may lead to disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.

sources.title: Acme Advisory Group — Company Overview
sources.content:
Who We Are

Acme Advisory Group is a management and technology consulting firm founded in 2011 in Karachi by Sara Qureshi and Daniel Okafor. Sara Qureshi serves as Chief Executive Officer and Daniel Okafor as Chief Financial Officer. The firm employs approximately 240 people across three offices: Karachi (headquarters), Dubai and London.

Practices

Acme is organised into three practices:

- Digital Transformation, led by Farah Naqvi, which redesigns operating models and customer journeys.
- Cloud Advisory, led by Mei Lin Zhou, who is also the firm's Chief Technology Officer. This practice runs Atlas, our managed client analytics platform.
- Risk and Compliance, led by Tomás Ferreira, who is also General Counsel. This practice helps clients prepare for ISO 27001 and SOC 2.

Clients and Sectors

We serve mid-sized organisations in logistics, healthcare and insurance. Our longest-running managed service is the Atlas analytics service for a European logistics client. Client names are confidential and are not published outside the firm.

Certifications

Acme has held ISO 27001 certification since 2019. The next recertification audit is scheduled for February 2027.

Leadership Team

|---|---|
| Chief Executive Officer | Sara Qureshi |
| Chief Financial Officer | Daniel Okafor |
| Chief Technology Officer | Mei Lin Zhou |
| Head of People (HR) | Priya Raman |

sources.title: Acme Service Catalog
sources.content:
Cloud Readiness Assessment

A four-week, fixed-fee engagement that reviews a client's applications, data and security posture and produces a migration roadmap. Delivered by the Cloud Advisory practice. Typical team: one manager and two consultants.

Atlas Managed Analytics

Atlas is Acme's managed analytics platform. Clients receive dashboards, data pipelines and a monthly insights review. Atlas is billed as a monthly subscription with a 99.5% availability commitment. Onboarding a new Atlas client takes six to eight weeks.

Cloud Migration Programmes

Multi-month programmes that move client workloads to the cloud. These are contracted under a Statement of Work (SOW) with milestone-based fees. Data residency requirements are agreed in the SOW before work starts.

Compliance Advisory

Gap assessments and remediation support for ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II. A gap assessment takes three weeks. Remediation support is billed on a time-and-materials basis at the consultant day rates published to clients each January.

Digital Operating Model Design

Workshops and design sprints that redesign how a client's teams work. Usually six to ten weeks.

How to Engage Us

New enquiries go to the engagement desk. A partner responds within two business days. Every engagement starts with a signed Master Services Agreement or a Statement of Work.

sources.title: Office Locations
sources.content:
Karachi (Headquarters)

Floor 7, Crescent Business Centre, Karachi. Around 150 staff. The Karachi office hosts the Digital Transformation practice, the People team and the finance team. Reception is staffed from 8:30 to 18:30.

Dubai

Level 12, Harbour Tower, Dubai Marina. Around 55 staff. Home of the Cloud Advisory practice and the Atlas operations team. The Dubai office also hosts the secondary Atlas operations room used during failover exercises.

London

3rd Floor, 22 Aldgate Row, London. Around 35 staff. The London office serves UK healthcare clients and hosts the Risk and Compliance practice.

Visiting Another Office

Staff visiting another office should book a desk through the facilities page at least two business days in advance. Building access cards are issued by the receiving office's facilities coordinator.

sources.title: Employee FAQ
sources.content:
What are standard office hours?

Core hours are 9:00 to 18:00 local time, Monday to Friday, in all three offices. Friday prayers are accommodated in Karachi and Dubai with a 12:30 to 14:00 break.

How do I get IT help?

Raise a ticket in Beacon, the internal IT helpdesk portal. Urgent issues (you cannot work at all) can also be reported to the IT hotline extension 4357. Beacon tickets are answered within four business hours.

How do I book business travel?

Travel is booked through the finance team using the travel request form in Ledgerline. Requests need line-manager approval before booking. See the Expense Policy for travel class rules.

Where are company policies kept?

All policies are published on the intranet under "Policies". HR policies such as leave and remote work are also in PeopleDesk, the HR portal.

Who do I contact about payroll?

Payroll questions go to the People team through PeopleDesk. Payslips are published on the 25th of each month.

Can I use personal devices for work?

Only for email and chat through the approved mobile apps, and only with device encryption and a screen lock enabled. Client data must never be stored on personal devices.

Full-time employees receive 22 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Up to five unused days can be carried over and must be used by 31 March of the following year.

3. Working Hours and Location > 3.4 Client Site Work

sources.title: Leave Policy
sources.content:
Scope

This policy applies to all permanent employees of Acme Advisory Group in Karachi, Dubai and London. Contractors follow the terms in their contracts. Where local employment law gives a more generous entitlement, local law applies. The policy is owned by Priya Raman, Head of People, and summarised in the Employee Handbook.

Annual Leave > Entitlement

Full-time employees receive 22 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement based on their contracted days. Employees who join or leave during the year receive a pro-rata entitlement for the months worked, rounded up to the nearest half day.

Annual Leave > Accrual

Annual leave accrues at 1.83 days per completed month of service. During probation, employees may take up to three days of accrued leave with their manager's approval.

Annual Leave > Carryover

Up to 5 unused days may be carried over into the next year. Carried-over days must be used by 31 March or they are forfeited. Unused leave beyond the five-day carryover is not paid out, except on leaving Acme.

Annual Leave > Requesting Annual Leave

Leave is requested in PeopleDesk, the HR portal. Requests for more than three consecutive days need at least two weeks' notice. The line manager approves or declines within three business days. If you work on a client engagement, also tell your engagement manager so that client cover can be arranged.

Annual Leave > Busy Periods

Managers may decline leave during critical client milestones, such as a planned cutover or a regulatory deadline, but must offer alternative dates. Platform engineers on the on-call rota must arrange a swap before taking leave during their on-call week.

sources.title: Expense Policy
sources.content:
Purpose

This policy explains which business expenses Globex reimburses, how to claim them and who approves them. It applies to all employees and partners. It is owned by Laura Bennett, CFO.

Submitting Claims

Claims are submitted in Claimly, the firm's expense app, within 45 days of the expense, with receipts. Claims submitted after 90 days are not reimbursed. Photograph paper receipts in the app; keep the originals for three months in case of an audit.

Approval Limits

- Up to USD 300: line manager.
- USD 300 to USD 3,000: director or partner.
- Above USD 3,000: Chief Financial Officer (Laura Bennett).

Approvers must not approve their own claims or claims for events they attended with the claimant; such claims go to the next level.

Travel > Flights

Economy class for all flights under eight hours. Premium economy may be booked for longer flights with partner approval. Flights are booked through the finance team, not by individuals.

Travel > Hotels

Hotels are booked through the finance team within the nightly limits published on the intranet for each city.

Travel > Per Diems

| Location | Per diem (USD per day) |
|---|---|
| Pakistan | 50 |
| UAE | 110 |
| United Kingdom | 100 |

Per diems cover meals and incidentals. Do not claim meals separately on days you claim a per diem.

Travel > Local Travel

Taxis and ride-hailing are reimbursed for client visits and for travel home after 22:00. During busy season, transport home after 22:00 is arranged by the office instead.

sources.title: Procurement Policy
sources.content:
Purpose and Scope

This policy makes sure Globex buys goods and services at fair prices from vendors that protect client data and do not threaten the firm's independence. It applies to all offices and all purchases. It is owned by Laura Bennett, CFO.

Purchase Requests

Purchases above USD 1,000 start with a purchase request approved by the budget holder. Smaller purchases may be made on a firm card and claimed in Claimly.

Quotes

Purchases above USD 5,000 need three quotes. Single-source purchases must be justified in writing and approved by the CFO.

Approval

Contracts above USD 25,000 per year need sign-off by a partner and the CFO. Contracts below that amount are approved by the budget holder. All contracts are reviewed by the Legal Counsel, Henrik Dahl, before signature.

Independence Checks

Because Globex is an audit firm, it must not enter business relationships with audit clients that could threaten independence. Before signing any contract, the finance team checks the vendor against the list of audit clients. sources.title: Audit Engagement Letter — Marlowe Retail Group plc
sources.content:
1. Introduction > 1.1 Parties

This engagement letter is between Globex Partners LLP ("Globex", "we" or "us"), an accounting and audit firm with offices in Lahore, Abu Dhabi and Manchester, and Marlowe Retail Group plc ("Marlowe", "the Company" or "you"), a UK retailer operating 186 stores and an online business.

1. Introduction > 1.2 Purpose

This letter confirms our appointment as statutory auditor of Marlowe Retail Group plc and its subsidiaries for the financial year ending 31 December 2026, and sets out the scope of our work, our respective responsibilities, the timetable, our fees and our terms of business.

1. Introduction > 1.3 Signature

This letter was signed on 2 March 2026 by Imran Siddiqui, Managing Partner, for Globex, and by Hannah Price, Chief Financial Officer, for Marlowe, on behalf of the board of directors. It was approved by Marlowe's audit committee, chaired by Peter Lawson, on 26 February 2026.

1. Introduction > 1.4 Continuing Relationship

Globex has audited Marlowe since the financial year ended 31 December 2023. This letter replaces the letter for the FY2025 audit, which ended when the FY2025 audit report was signed on 1 April 2026.

2. Scope of the Audit > 2.1 Statutory Audit

We will audit the consolidated and parent company financial statements of Marlowe for the year ending 31 December 2026, in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (UK) and applicable law. Our objective is to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor's report that includes our opinion.

Appendix M — Interim Findings Summary (October 2026)

Interim fieldwork in August 2026 found that the new point-of-sale system's interface to the general ledger had run without failures since go-live, but that user access reviews for the point-of-sale system had not yet been performed. The review control for manual journals introduced in June 2026 was operating, with two exceptions out of 25 samples where the reviewer was also the preparer. Both matters were reported to the audit committee on 21 October 2026. Neither changes the fee at this stage.

Appendix N — Contacts for Ledger Vault Problems

If Marlowe's users cannot upload or access files in Ledger Vault, they should contact James Whitaker, who will raise a ticket with Globex's IT service desk (extension 2020). sources.content:
**Where may Halvorsen data be stored?** Only in Cobalt Cloud's Frankfurt region, with the disaster recovery replica in Dubai (clause 9.2). Never copy Halvorsen data to the London region, to laptops or to other tools.

2. Objectives

The Trust wants to retire two ageing on-premises systems hosted in its own data centre, whose hardware support ends in March 2027:

- PatientFlow, the patient scheduling system used by all clinics and outpatient departments.

sources.content:
22. Options for Hosting After Handover

The steering committee considered three options for hosting after the SOW ends:

1. **The Trust contracts directly with Cobalt Cloud.** The Trust would need its own agreement covering the London region, data processing terms and support. Cobalt has offered terms, but the Trust's procurement process may take three months.
2. **Acme provides a managed hosting service.** Acme would keep the Trust account under CC-ENT-4471 and charge a monthly managed service fee. This depends on Acme's renewal with Cobalt, which must be signed by 30 November 2026.
3. **Short-term bridge.** Acme continues hosting at cost for up to six months while the Trust completes its own procurement.

The committee chose option 3 as a bridge, with a decision between options 1 and 2 by March 2027. The bridge will be documented in a short change request to this SOW, and the Trust's Data Protection Officer has confirmed that the existing data processing terms continue to apply during the bridge period.

23. Lessons From the Atlas Outage Applied to This SOW

After Acme's March 2026 Atlas outage, the Trust asked how a similar hosting failure would affect PatientFlow. Because cross-region failover is not allowed under the data residency terms, the design uses three availability zones within the London region for the PatientFlow database and application tier, and the failover procedure between zones was tested in pre-production before cutover.

Marlowe recognises online revenue on delivery and records a provision for expected returns. Marlowe plans to close 14 stores in 2027. We will attend inventory counts at 12 sampled stores, including at least three scheduled for closure, and test whether inventory in those stores is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value, taking into account expected clearance discounts.

We will review management's impairment model for underperforming stores, challenge the cash flow forecasts against 2026 actual results, and test the discount rate with the help of our valuation specialists in the Manchester office.

We will test journal entries using data analytics across the full population of 2026 journals, focusing on manual entries posted after 31 December, entries posted by senior management, and entries to revenue and provisions.

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Summary > What Happened

On Monday 30 March 2026, during the last week of busy season, Ledger Vault, Globex's client document portal, was unavailable for 6 hours 10 minutes (370 minutes), from 09:05 to 15:15 PKT. The incident was classified Severity 1. The incident commander was Kwame Mensah, Head of IT.

Summary > Why It Happened

The Ledger Vault metadata database ran out of storage after a surge of client uploads in the final days of busy season. Storage alerts were set at 95% of capacity and fired too late to act before the disk filled. Once the disk was full, the database stopped accepting writes and the application could not serve any page that needed a session record. A storage resize request to Tessera Cloud, the hosting provider, took 2 hours 40 minutes.

Summary > Status

This postmortem is blameless. All five action items are complete.

Impact > Client and Engagement Impact

Audit teams could not download client evidence or upload working-paper attachments for the whole outage. Clients could not upload documents. Several December year-end audits were in their final day of fieldwork, including the FY2025 audit of Marlowe Retail Group plc, a UK retailer. Two audit report sign-offs, including Marlowe's, were delayed by one day; Marlowe's FY2025 audit report was signed on 1 April 2026 instead of 31 March.

No client files were lost. Uploads attempted during the outage failed with an error and had to be repeated.

Impact > Internal Impact

About 120 audit staff in Lahore, Abu Dhabi and Manchester were unable to work on evidence for most of the day. Engagement managers moved teams to review work in Fernbook that did not need new evidence.

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Appendix C — Glossary

- Metadata database: the PostgreSQL database that stores file records, versions, permissions and sessions for Ledger Vault. Client files themselves are in object storage.
- Write-ahead log: the database's record of changes, replayed during recovery.
- Busy season: 15 January to 31 March, when most December year-end audits are completed.
- TC-7720: Globex's agreement reference with Tessera Cloud.
- TES-55190: Tessera's ticket reference for the urgent resize request.

Appendix D — Text of the Client Apology (31 March 2026)

"Dear client, on Monday 30 March, Ledger Vault, our secure document portal, was unavailable from 09:05 to 15:15 Pakistan time. During that period you could not upload or view documents, and our audit teams could not access evidence. No documents were lost, and documents you tried to upload during the outage should now be uploaded again. The cause was a storage capacity issue in our hosting environment, which has now been fixed, and we have added automatic capacity scaling and earlier warnings so that it cannot happen in the same way again. Where this affected your audit timetable, your engagement partner will contact you directly. We apologise for the disruption at the busiest time of the year. Imran Siddiqui, Managing Partner."

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Appendix N — Lessons Shared With Other Teams

The finance team learned that the Tessera claim window is only 15 days and now records claim deadlines in the vendor register. The audit methodology team added a step to the busy-season plan: engagement managers agree with clients, before final fieldwork, which documents are needed in the last week, so that a portal outage on the final day has less impact. HR added a note to the Staff Handbook's busy-season guide on what to do if Ledger Vault is unavailable.

Appendix O — Who Was Involved

| Person | Role in the incident |
|---|---|
| Kwame Mensah | Head of IT; incident commander |
| Two IT engineers | Diagnosis, cleanup of expired sessions, recovery monitoring |
| Tessera account engineer | Completed the resize under TES-55190 |
| Laura Bennett | CFO; filed the Service Credit claim on 8 April 2026 |
| Imran Siddiqui | Managing Partner; sent the client apology on 31 March 2026 |
| Nadia Hussain | Engagement partner for Marlowe Retail Group; agreed the one-day delay to the FY2025 report |
| Henrik Dahl | Legal Counsel; confirmed no client breach notification was required |

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
**Should Globex keep Ledger Vault in-house?** The partners agreed to keep Ledger Vault, because it gives clients a single secure place to share evidence and integrates with Fernbook, but asked IT to report on the renewal options with Tessera before the notice deadline of 30 January 2027.

**Could clients have been told sooner?** Yes. The first client communication was at 13:30, more than four hours into the outage. The IT on-call guide now requires engagement partners to be informed within 30 minutes of a Sev1 affecting Ledger Vault, so they can contact clients with imminent deadlines.

**Was any client data at risk?** No. The failure prevented writes but did not corrupt or expose data. The Legal Counsel confirmed that no client notification under the engagement letters' breach clauses was needed.

**What happens if this repeats during the 2027 busy season?** Automatic scaling, earlier alerts and the December capacity review should prevent a repeat. If Ledger Vault is unavailable for more than four hours during final fieldwork, engagement letters such as Marlowe's now allow a temporary encrypted transfer approved by the Head of IT, keeping UK files in the UK.

sources.title: Postmortem: Ledger Vault Outage, 30 March 2026
sources.content:
Timeline (all times PKT) > Outage

- 30 March, 09:05: database storage reaches 100%. The database stops accepting writes. Ledger Vault returns errors for all users.
- 09:12: service desk receives the first calls from audit teams.
- 09:20: Severity 1 declared. Kwame Mensah takes incident command.
- 09:35: cause identified as a full database disk.
- 09:42: urgent storage resize requested from Tessera, ticket TES-55190, raised as Priority 2 because the support portal classified resize requests as changes.
- 10:30: no progress on the ticket. Globex escalates by phone and the ticket is raised to Priority 1.
- 10:45: IT team deletes 40 GB of expired session logs to free space, but the database will not restart writes until it has 5% free.
- 12:22: Tessera completes the resize from 500 GB to 750 GB, 2 hours 40 minutes after the request.
- 12:30 to 14:50: database recovery runs. The database replays its write-ahead log and runs integrity checks, which take longer than expected because of the volume of recent writes.
- 15:15: Ledger Vault available again for all users.
- 15:40: Engagement partners informed that service has been restored.

Root Cause Analysis > Primary Cause

The metadata database was provisioned with 500 GB of storage in April 2024 and had not been resized. Upload volumes grew 60% year on year, mainly because more clients used Ledger Vault instead of email during busy season.

Scope

This policy applies to all permanent employees of Acme Advisory Group in Karachi, Dubai and London. Contractors follow the terms in their contracts. Where local employment law gives a more generous entitlement, local law applies. The policy is owned by Priya Raman, Head of People, and summarised in the Employee Handbook.

Annual Leave > Entitlement

Full-time employees receive 22 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement based on their contracted days. Employees who join or leave during the year receive a pro-rata entitlement for the months worked, rounded up to the nearest half day.

Annual Leave > Accrual

Annual leave accrues at 1.83 days per completed month of service. During probation, employees may take up to three days of accrued leave with their manager's approval.

Annual Leave > Carryover

Up to 5 unused days may be carried over into the next year. Carried-over days must be used by 31 March or they are forfeited. Unused leave beyond the five-day carryover is not paid out, except on leaving Acme.

Annual Leave > Requesting Annual Leave

Leave is requested in PeopleDesk, the HR portal. Requests for more than three consecutive days need at least two weeks' notice. The line manager approves or declines within three business days. If you work on a client engagement, also tell your engagement manager so that client cover can be arranged.

Annual Leave > Busy Periods

Managers may decline leave during critical client milestones, such as a planned cutover or a regulatory deadline, but must offer alternative dates. Platform engineers on the on-call rota must arrange a swap before taking leave during their on-call week.

A consultant on the Brightwater Health Trust migration requests leave over the PatientFlow cutover weekend. The engagement manager may decline because it is a critical client milestone, but must offer alternative dates.

sources.title: Runbook: Atlas Database Failover
sources.content:
When to Use

Use this runbook when the primary Atlas PostgreSQL cluster in Frankfurt is unavailable or read-only for more than 10 minutes and Cobalt Cloud cannot give a recovery estimate within that time. Revised on 2 April 2026 for platform version 4.2 after the March outage (action item ATL-1121), and tested in the Q2 and Q3 2026 drills.

Targets

Recovery point objective: 5 minutes. Recovery time objective: 30 minutes. These targets appear in the Halvorsen Logistics MSA, so every failover must be recorded for client reporting.

Roles

- Incident commander: coordinates and decides go/no-go for promotion.
- Operator: runs the commands in this runbook.
- Communications lead: updates the status page within 15 minutes and every 30 minutes after, and emails Halvorsen's operations team hourly.

One person must not hold more than one role during a Severity 1 incident.

Pre-Checks

1. Declare a Severity 1 incident in PagerDuty and page the incident commander on duty.
2. Open a Priority 1 ticket with Cobalt Cloud support, quoting enterprise agreement CC-ENT-4471. Record the Cobalt incident reference; finance needs it to claim a Service Credit.
3. Check Cobalt's status portal for the Frankfurt region and note the start time of the incident.
4. In Grafana, confirm replication lag on the Dubai replica is under 5 minutes. If it is higher, the incident commander decides whether to wait or accept the data loss, and records the decision.

The MSA treats the recovery objectives as targets rather than as commitments that carry Service Credits, but the miss was reported to Halvorsen in the written incident report as required by clause 7.3 of the MSA.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
**Could we have avoided the outage entirely?** Not the storage failure, which was Cobalt's. But with an up-to-date runbook and a recent drill, recovery would probably have taken about 30 minutes instead of 220.

**Did we breach the Halvorsen MSA?** No. Availability stayed above 99.5%. We missed the 30-minute recovery time objective, which the MSA states as a target, and we reported that openly.

**What would it take to fail over automatically?** Automatic promotion would need a reliable way to decide that Frankfurt is truly down, to avoid two primaries. The platform team recommends finishing multi-zone placement first, which addresses the most likely failure mode, and revisiting automatic failover in 2027.

**Does this affect the Cobalt renewal?** Yes. The renewal term sheet now asks for multi-zone placement for managed PostgreSQL at no extra charge and a 60-day Service Credit claim window.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
SLA Calculations > Atlas Availability for Halvorsen

March 2026 had 31 days, which is 44,640 minutes. Downtime was 220 minutes. Availability was therefore (44,640 − 220) ÷ 44,640 = 99.507%, reported as 99.51%. The Halvorsen MSA threshold is 99.5%, so no Service Credit was due. The largest outage that would have stayed above 99.5% in March is 223 minutes.

SLA Calculations > Cobalt Cloud Availability for Acme

Cobalt measured Frankfurt region availability at 99.51% for March. The CC-ENT-4471 threshold is 99.9%, so the Frankfurt region earned the 10% Service Credit tier (below 99.9% but at least 99.0%). March's Frankfurt Regional Fees were EUR 16,500, so the credit was EUR 1,650. The Dubai and London regions were unaffected and earned no credit.

Follow-Up Failover Drills > Q2 2026 Drill (12 May 2026)

The rewritten runbook was used to fail Atlas over from Frankfurt to Dubai in a planned drill during the Sunday maintenance window. Failover completed in 19 minutes, inside the 30-minute recovery time objective. One issue was found: the configuration service cached the old database endpoint for five minutes. The cache time was reduced to 30 seconds.

Follow-Up Failover Drills > Q3 2026 Drill (9 August 2026)

The drill was run by a newer engineer who had never performed a failover, to test whether the runbook could be followed without help. Failover completed in 24 minutes. The drill summary was shared with Halvorsen Logistics, as the MSA requires on request.

sources.title: Postmortem: Atlas Outage, 14 March 2026
sources.content:
What Happened

On Saturday 14 March 2026, Atlas was unavailable to all clients for 3 hours 40 minutes (220 minutes), from 06:10 to 09:50 UTC. The incident was classified Severity 1. The incident commander was Bilal Ahmed, with Mei Lin Zhou (CTO) as the executive on call.

Why It Happened

A storage incident in Cobalt Cloud's Frankfurt region made the primary Atlas PostgreSQL cluster read-only. The team tried to fail over to the disaster recovery replica in the Dubai region, but the database failover runbook was out of date: it referenced a replication setting that had been renamed in the January 2026 platform upgrade. Working out the correct procedure under pressure took about two hours.

Status

This postmortem is blameless. All action items are tracked in Jira under the epic ATL-1120. As of 30 June 2026, five of seven action items are complete.

sources.title: Atlas Platform Architecture
sources.content:
Deployment

Code is hosted in GitHub Enterprise and deployed by GitHub Actions. Production deployments need one approving review and run only between 10:00 and 16:00 PKT on weekdays. Platform upgrades follow a checklist that, since April 2026, includes reviewing every runbook affected by the change.

Security

All data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Production access requires SSO with hardware-key multi-factor authentication. Access is reviewed quarterly by the platform team. An independent penetration test of Atlas is commissioned every year, as required by client contracts and by Acme's ISO 27001 certification.

Recovery

The database failover runbook describes how to promote the Dubai replica. Failover drills run every quarter; the Q2 2026 drill completed in 19 minutes and the Q3 2026 drill in 24 minutes, both within the 30-minute recovery time objective.

Known Limitations

- Single-zone primary database until ATL-1125 is complete.
- Staging database configuration differs from production (ATL-1127, not started).
- Cross-region failover is manual; there is no automatic promotion.

sources.title: Code Of Conduct
sources.content:
Acme Advisory Group expects every employee to act with integrity, respect and care for client confidentiality.

Gifts and hospitality: employees may accept gifts worth up to USD 50. Anything above USD 50 must be declared to the compliance team within five business days and may need to be returned.

Conflicts of interest: any personal or financial relationship with a client, supplier or competitor must be declared to your line manager and the General Counsel before you work on a related engagement.

Confidentiality: client information may only be shared with colleagues who need it for their work. Client data must stay within approved systems.

Speaking up: concerns can be raised confidentially with the General Counsel, Tomás Ferreira, or through the anonymous ethics line. Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith is a disciplinary offence.

Breaches of this code may lead to disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.

sources.title: Acme Service Catalog
sources.content:
Cloud Readiness Assessment

A four-week, fixed-fee engagement that reviews a client's applications, data and security posture and produces a migration roadmap. Delivered by the Cloud Advisory practice. Typical team: one manager and two consultants.

Atlas Managed Analytics

Atlas is Acme's managed analytics platform. Clients receive dashboards, data pipelines and a monthly insights review. Atlas is billed as a monthly subscription with a 99.5% availability commitment. Onboarding a new Atlas client takes six to eight weeks.

Cloud Migration Programmes

Multi-month programmes that move client workloads to the cloud. These are contracted under a Statement of Work (SOW) with milestone-based fees. Data residency requirements are agreed in the SOW before work starts.

Compliance Advisory

Gap assessments and remediation support for ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II. A gap assessment takes three weeks. Remediation support is billed on a time-and-materials basis at the consultant day rates published to clients each January.

Digital Operating Model Design

Workshops and design sprints that redesign how a client's teams work. Usually six to ten weeks.

How to Engage Us

New enquiries go to the engagement desk. A partner responds within two business days. Every engagement starts with a signed Master Services Agreement or a Statement of Work.

sources.title: Employee FAQ

What are standard office hours?

Core hours are 9:00 to 18:00 local time, Monday to Friday, in all three offices. Friday prayers are accommodated in Karachi and Dubai with a 12:30 to 14:00 break.

How do I get IT help?

Raise a ticket in Beacon, the internal IT helpdesk portal. Urgent issues (you cannot work at all) can also be reported to the IT hotline extension 4357. Beacon tickets are answered within four business hours.

How do I book business travel?

Travel is booked through the finance team using the travel request form in Ledgerline. Requests need line-manager approval before booking. See the Expense Policy for travel class rules.

Where are company policies kept?

All policies are published on the intranet under "Policies". HR policies such as leave and remote work are also in PeopleDesk, the HR portal.

Who do I contact about payroll?
